resources.string: Format JSON or validate XML and lay out its attributes locally.

Choose JSON or XML. JSON supports validation, pretty-printing and minification; XML supports validation or conservative attribute layout. Explicitly run the operation. Processing stays local; automatic history and result saving are off by default.
Try a small object with a name string and an enabled boolean, then explicitly format or validate it.

JSON and XML 1.0 only, not CSS or HTML. XML rejects DTDs and external entities; formatting preserves content and changes only attribute layout, not tree indentation. Duplicate object keys are rejected rather than silently overwritten. Input and nesting limits apply. Valid syntax does not prove data is safe or matches a schema; review before copying or sharing private content.
Load a small object with a name string and an enabled boolean, then explicitly run pretty-printing.
